title: Gwinnett couple warn others after losing $800K in cryptocurrency scam

reading.body:
A retired Georgia couple lost nearly $800,000 to a cryptocurrency scam that exploited trust built gradually over time. A scammer contacted them via WhatsApp and directed them to a mobile trading app, then created a fake overlay on their screen showing false account balances and fabricated returns. The victim made progressively larger investments based on what appeared to be successful trades, only discovering the fraud when attempting to withdraw funds.

This is a case of an impersonation attack layered on top of a legitimate application. The scammers did not compromise the trading app itself, but instead inserted a fraudulent interface between the victim and the real platform. The failure occurred at the point of user verification: no system checked whether the person accessing the account was actually its owner, and no confirmation process interrupted the withdrawal when it contradicted the fake overlay the victim saw.

It is not established whether the trading app had security features that could have detected the overlay, whether the victim received warnings about unusual account activity, or what technical measures might have prevented the fake interface from operating.

reports.title: Georgia couple loses $800K in sophisticated cryptocurrency scam
Gwinnett couple warn others after losing $800K in cryptocurrency scam

summary:
A retired Georgia couple lost nearly $800,000 in a sophisticated cryptocurrency scam that started with a WhatsApp message from a stranger. The scammer convinced Jerry Dunaway to invest in cryptocurrency through a mobile trading app, gradually building trust by allowing him to make small trades and withdraw modest amounts. Over time, Jerry increased his investments, believing he was seeing legitimate returns on the platform.

The scam unraveled when Jerry tried to withdraw a larger sum and discovered he couldn't access the funds. Police determined that while the trading app itself was real, scammers had created a fake overlay that showed false account information on Jerry's screen. The couple, Jerry and Mindy Dunaway, are now working with Gwinnett County police but have been warned that victims in these cases rarely recover their stolen money. Their children have started a GoFundMe campaign to help them with daily expenses, and the Dunaways are speaking publicly to warn others about these elaborate schemes.
